quote: The X-Robots-Tag response header defines how crawlers should index URLs.
While not part of any specification, it is a de-facto standard method for communicating with search bots, web crawlers, and similar user agents.
Search-related crawlers use the rules from the X-Robots-Tag header to adjust how to present web pages or other resources in search results.
Specifying indexing rules in an HTTP header is useful for non-HTML documents like images, PDFs, or other media.
Only cooperative robots follow these rules, and a crawler first needs to access the resource to read headers and meta elements
An optional <bot-name>: specifies the user agent that the subsequent rules should apply to:
X-Robots-Tag: <indexing-rule>, …, <indexing-ruleN>
X-Robots-Tag: <bot-name>: <indexing-rule>, …, <indexing-ruleN>
Any of the following indexing rules may be used:
No restrictions for indexing or serving in search results.
This rule is the default value and has no effect if explicitly listed.
Equivalent to noindex, nofollow.
indexifembedded only has an effect if it's accompanied by noindex.
Ignored if no valid <number> is specified.
A larger image preview, up to the width of the viewport, may be shown.
No video length limit.
A date must be specified in a format such as RFC 822, RFC 850, or ISO 8601.
In the case of conflicting robot rules within the X-Robots-Tag or between the X-Robots-Tag HTTP header and the <meta name="robots"> element
the more restrictive rule applies.
Some values are mutually exclusive, such as index and noindex, or follow and nofollow.
In these cases, the crawler's behavior is undefined and may vary.
The following response has two X-Robots-Tag headers, each with an indexing rule specified:
X-Robots-Tag: noimageindex
X-Robots-Tag: unavailable_after: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 13:09:53 GMT
Each indexing rule applies to the user agent specified behind it:
X-Robots-Tag: BadBot: noindex, nofollow, googlebot: nofollow
For situations where multiple crawlers are specified along with different rules, the search engine will use the sum of the negative rules.
Not part of any current specification.
This page was last modified on Aug 21, 2026 by MDN contributors.
To block indexing of non-HTML resources, such as PDF files, video files, or image files, use the X-Robots-Tag response header instead.
The X-Robots-Tag can be used as an element of the HTTP header response for a given URL.
Any rule that can be used in a robots meta tag can also be specified as an X-Robots-Tag.
Multiple X-Robots-Tag headers can be combined within the HTTP response, or you can specify a comma-separated list of rules.
The X-Robots-Tag may optionally specify a user agent before the rules.
Rules specified without a user agent are valid for all crawlers.
The HTTP header, the user agent name, and the specified values are not case sensitive.
In the case of conflicting robots rules, the more restrictive rule applies.
X-Robots-Tag: unavailable_after: 25 Jun 2010 15:00:00 PST
This document specifies and extends the "Robots Exclusion Protocol" method originally defined by Martijn Koster in 1994
The protocol language consists of rule(s) and group(s) that the service makes available in a file named "robots.txt"
These rules are not a form of access authorization.
